message: the walk reached a tag at offset 301 (`<span class="pct-marker__badge">`) and the tag reader did not
$reason: Two tags in the `@placeholder` of a deferred block, read by a tag reader that does not descend into a placeholder: an override of the reader's that forgets `super`, played by the visit it makes today — the walk's `"sides": { "drop" }` turned round. The walk reaches both through the side block it is handed and gives each a path; the reader records neither, so what makes either a stop would go unread, and point 1 refuses the first of them by its offset and its opening tag: the badge, not the dot after it. No template reaches this refusal by itself, which is why the reader is doctored and not the text: the walk gives a path only to an element it reaches through children, branches and side blocks, and the reader, the compiler's own visitor, meets every element, template and projection. `visit` stands beside it and takes nothing, since the hook takes only a visit: let through, it would take every visit — Angular's `visitAll` calls a visitor's `visit` in place of each node's own — and the refusal would name the first template's first tag. Pinned, the message holds the refusal and the tag it names; without the case, the refusal taken out or naming the last tag still passed every prepared input.
